cohort: The study included 106,760 migrant women and 473,881 Swedish-born women having singleton, first births.
finding: Longer duration of residence in Sweden was associated with an increased overall risk of both unplanned and planned caesarean section among migrant women, even after adjusting for social, obstetric, and health factors.
mod_finding: The risk of both unplanned and planned caesarean section tended to increase with length of residence among migrant women.
